events.text: {npc} has gone grey at the temples. You notice it all at once, over dinner, and cannot stop noticing.

effects.log: {He} laughs and says you are a terrible liar. {He} is pleased anyway.
You carry the water and chop the wood from now on. {He} pretends not to notice.

events.text: {npc} takes you out to the fields at dawn and, for once, has something to say.

effects.log: 'Be the kind of person people are glad to see coming,' {he} says. That is all. It is enough.
{He} tells you about a girl, a river and a fight {he} lost. You see {him} differently.

events.text: {npc} insists on teaching you {his} three best recipes 'before I forget them'.

effects.log: You burn the first, ruin the second and nail the third. {He} cries a little.
You write them on good paper. {He} keeps the paper in {his} altar box.

events.text: You learn {npc} has been quietly paying off a debt for years, to a man who cheated {him}.

effects.log: The man is surprised to see you. The debt is closed. {npc} never mentions it, and never forgets.

ok.log: The cheat forgives the rest, faced with your stare.

fail.log: The cheat laughs. {npc} asks you to leave it be.

events.text: {npc} is sick this winter, coughing through the nights, and still insists on getting up to cook.

effects.log: Broth, blankets and bad jokes. {He} recovers by spring.
The physician is expensive and effective. {npc} scolds you for the cost.

events.text: {npc} tells every neighbour about your latest deeds, adding a few details that never happened.

effects.log: Your legend grows in the village. So does {his} happiness.
'Let an old parent have this,' says a neighbour. You let it go.

events.text: {npc} has invited a 'friend's child' to dinner. It is very obviously a marriage interview.

effects.log: The guest is lovely and equally trapped. You laugh about it together afterwards.
{npc} is furious, then laughing. The guest fled too.

events.text: {npc} brings out an old sword from under the bed. 'I was going to be a swordsman, once. Then you were born.'

choices.text: Ask {him} to show you a form

effects.log: {His} knees creak and {his} form is old-fashioned and beautiful.
'It is only iron,' {he} says, and gives it to you anyway.

events.text: A letter from {npc} reaches you far from home, the brushwork shakier than you remember.

effects.log: You write three pages. {He} reads them aloud to the whole village.
Weeks of travel for a week at home. {He} does not stop smiling.

events.text: {npc} disapproves of your life in the murim, loudly, in front of the neighbours.

mem.note: argued in front of the neighbours

effects.log: Doors slam. You are both right. You are both miserable for a week.
Under the shouting is fear. You promise to be careful. {He} goes quiet.

events.text: {npc} is very old now and very tired. {He} asks you to sit by the bed and talk about nothing.

mem.note: sat with me at the end

effects.log: {He} falls asleep smiling, holding your hand.
It all comes out. {He} listens, and forgives all of it.

events.text: {npc} never says {he} is proud of you. Today you find {his} notes: every one of your deeds, written down year by year.

effects.log: You put the book back exactly where it was. You feel ten feet tall.
{He} goes red and says it was the neighbours who kept the notes. It was not.

events.text: {npc} tells you about the famine of {his} childhood, when the whole village ate tree bark for a winter.

effects.log: You never waste rice again.
{He} eats it slowly, like a treasure.

events.text: {npc} teaches you xiangqi and cheats shamelessly.

ok.log: {He} laughs so hard {he} coughs. 'Finally, a clever one.'

fail.log: {He} wins forty games in a row. You suspect nothing.

effects.log: {He} knows. {He} appreciates it anyway.

events.text: {npc} knows every herb in the hills and is determined that someone will remember them after {he} is gone.

effects.log: A summer of walking the hills with {him}. You know sixty herbs by autumn.
{He} talks, you carry. It is a good summer.

events.text: {npc} has been told for the tenth time this month to 'be more like you'. {He} is not happy about it.

effects.log: {npc} stares at you, then laughs. It is the start of something better.
{npc} hides your shoes for a month.

events.text: {npc} confesses a secret: {he} is in love with someone the family will never approve of.

effects.log: You stand guard at a lot of bridges at night.
{He} is careful for about a week.

events.text: {npc} asks to borrow money 'for a business idea'. {His} last business idea was ducks.

effects.log: The ducks, it turns out, were a good idea. {He} repays you double. (+20 taels)

mem.note: did not believe in my ducks

effects.log: {He} sulks, then finds the money elsewhere. The ducks do well without you.

events.text: {npc} is getting married, and asks you to lead the procession.

effects.log: Drums, red silk and your best clothes. {npc} cries through the whole ceremony.
An expensive gift. {npc} would have preferred you.

events.text: You and {npc} fight like children over something neither of you remembers by the evening.

effects.log: {He} apologises second. You both go fishing.
A week of silence. In the end, hunger makes you both apologise at the same dinner.

events.text: {npc} wants to join the murim too, and asks you to teach {him}.

effects.log: A year of lessons. {He} is better than you expected and worse than {he} thinks.

mem.note: talked me out of the murim

effects.log: 'One of us should live long,' you say. {He} is angry, then grateful.

events.text: {npc} and you are old now. You sit on the porch and argue about who broke the rice jar a lifetime ago.

effects.log: {He} gasps. 'I KNEW it!' A lifetime of suspicion, resolved.
Neither of you owned a dog. The argument continues until dinner.

events.text: A quiet morning. {npc} brings you tea and sits beside you without a word, watching the rain.

mem.note: held my hand in the rain

effects.log: Nothing else happens. It is one of the best mornings of your life.
{He} listens, then tells you {his}. You didn't know.

events.text: {npc} has heard a rumour that you have been seen walking with someone else.

ok.log: It was a merchant asking directions. {He} laughs at {him}self.

mem.note: did not explain the rumour well

fail.log: Your explanation sounds guilty even to you. A cold week.

effects.log: You walk everywhere together for a month. The gossips give up.

events.text: {npc} falls ill, and for the first time in years you are afraid of something you cannot fight.

effects.log: Days and nights. {He} recovers slowly, and never forgets who stayed.
Three days' ride. The physician comes. {He} recovers.

events.text: {npc} wants to plant a garden: vegetables, a plum tree, and a bench 'for when we are old'.

effects.log: A spring of digging. The plum tree blooms the next year.
It wobbles. {He} loves it.

events.text: {npc} found out how much you spent on a new sword. {He} is holding the receipt like a verdict.

effects.log: The old sword is fine. The marriage is better.
A long week. The sword is very good, at least.

events.text: You and {npc} are grey now. Children run past the gate. {He} says: 'We were that fast once.'

effects.log: Neither of you runs. You walk very fast and call it a tie.

choices.text: Say you are still that fast

effects.log: {He} laughs until {he} has to sit down.

events.text: You discover that {npc} can throw a knife across a courtyard into a coin. {He} never mentioned it.

effects.log: 'Before I met you,' {he} says, and smiles, and changes the subject. Forever.
You learn more about {him} in a month of knife-throwing than in years of marriage.

events.text: {npc} says {his} first word. It is not your name.

effects.log: It was "rice". You tell everyone it was your name.
By the end of the month {he} says it constantly, at dawn, loudly.

events.text: {npc}, barely walking, has taken your sword off the wall and is dragging it across the courtyard.

effects.log: {He} will not let go of it for three years.
{He} builds a staircase out of the furniture. You are in trouble.

events.text: {npc} comes home from school crying: the other children call {him} the child of a 'murim thug'.

effects.log: You walk {him} to the door. Nobody says anything, ever again.
'My parent protects all of you,' {he} says the next day. It works.

events.text: At the temple fair, {npc} vanishes into the crowd. Your heart stops.

ok.log: You find {him} watching the puppet show, entirely calm.

fail.log: An hour of terror. {He} was at the sweet stall the whole time.

effects.log: From the top of the gate you spot {him} at once, eating a candied hawthorn.

events.text: {npc} announces {he} will never join the murim, never marry, and will become a travelling poet.

effects.log: {He} is so surprised {he} forgets to rebel for a month.
Slammed doors for a year. {He} becomes a poet anyway, a good one.

events.text: {npc} comes home with a split lip and a very proud face. 'You should see the other one.'

effects.log: A bully, a smaller child and your child in between. You are very proud.
A month of dawn lessons. The bully never tries again.

events.text: {npc} is grown, packing a bag at the gate. {He} is going out into the world, as you once did.

mem.note: gave me advice at the gate

effects.log: 'Eat well. Trust slowly. Come home.' {He} laughs, then hugs you too long.

mem.note: gave me silver for the road

effects.log: Fifty taels in a cloth bundle. {He} will need it.

events.text: {npc} brings someone home for dinner. They are both very nervous.

effects.log: By the end of dinner they are both laughing. A wedding follows in spring.
An hour of questions. The newcomer answers them all. You approve, secretly.

events.text: A letter from {npc}, grown now and far away. 'I did something you would be proud of. I thought of you the whole time.'

choices.text: Write back how proud you are

effects.log: {He} keeps your letter all {his} life.
A long journey to see {him} for a week. {He} shows you everything.

events.text: {npc} insists on carrying your things now, and walking on the side of the road where the carts pass.

mem.note: let me take care of them

effects.log: The circle turns. You remember carrying {him}.
{He} carries them anyway. You are secretly glad.
